html:
The Gaambera are an Aboriginal people of the far north Kimberley in Western Australia, on the rugged coast and islands near Admiralty Gulf. Their language, Gamberre or Gaambera, is a dialect of Wunambal, one of the Worrorran languages.

They are closely tied to the Wunambal people next door, and the two now hold native title together as Wunambal Gaambera. Their country is known for its rock art, above all the Wandjina, the painted cloud and rain spirits of the Worrorran peoples. Neighbours included the Miwa and the Kwini to the east.

This remote coast saw little of Europeans until well into the 1900s. The language is now spoken by only a few people, and a revival project began in the 2010s. See Aboriginal Australian societies for the wider story.
